pages.quiz:
HOME SCIENCE MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pastry Making.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting.

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Care of the Home: Exterior Environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Consumer Protection and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.

4. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

6. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

8. D — Producers

9. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

10. A — 100 °C

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.

12. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Care of the Home: Exterior Environment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Consumer Protection; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
